title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 5.1.3 Positive Usage of Media

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Media are the ways we receive and share information, such as books, newspapers, radio, television, mobile phones and the Internet. Media can help us learn and grow closer to Allah (S.W.T.), or they can harm us if used wrongly. In this sub-strand you will identify types of media, learn how to use them positively and follow Islamic manners when using them.

## Strand 5.0: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Sub-strand 5.1.3: Positive Usage of Media
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify types of media that can be used to reinforce learning
b) explain the positive use of media for Islamic character formation
c) observe Islamic ethics while using media in day-to-day life
d) appreciate media as a gift from Allah (S.W.T.) by using them appropriately

## Key inquiry questions
1. What types of media do you use at home?
2. How can you use media positively?
3. How can you use media while observing Islamic teachings?

## Core competencies
• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with digital technology enhanced as learners watch video clips on positive use of media.
• Communication: the skill of listening is enhanced as learners listen to a resource person discussing the Islamic teachings governing the use of media.
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners take turns to discuss the positive and negative uses of media.

## Values
• Responsibility is enhanced as learners discuss the positive and negative uses of media, in pairs/ groups, and present in class.
• Integrity is enhanced as learners listen to a resource person discussing the Islamic teachings governing the use of media.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Assertiveness in the proper use of the media.

## Links to other learning areas
• Science and Technology: as learners search, download and store information from the internet.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings), Sub-strand 5.1.3 Positive Usage of Media
• Qur’an 96:4-5; Qur’an 49:6; Qur’an 17:36
• Sahih al-Bukhari: two blessings (health and free time); Bukhari and Muslim: say what is good or keep silent; Jami at-Tirmidhi: leaving what does not concern him

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Types of media that help us learn

LESSON 1: TYPES OF MEDIA THAT HELP US LEARN
===========================================

## What you will learn
• Name the main types of media.
• Give examples of how each type of media can help a learner.
• Explain why media are a gift from Allah (S.W.T.).

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify types of media that can be used to reinforce learning; d) appreciate media as a gift from Allah (S.W.T.) by using them appropriately

## Introduction
At home you may listen to a Qur’an recitation on the radio, watch the news on television or read a storybook. All these are media. Which ones do you use at home?

## Notes
### What are media?
Media are tools and channels that carry information, messages, sounds and pictures from one person to many people.

### Types of media
- Print media: books, newspapers, magazines, posters and charts. Examples: your IRE course book, a Qur’an mushaf, a Madrasa textbook.
- Broadcast media: television, radio and movies. Examples: Islamic programmes on radio or TV, lessons for learners on educational radio and TV.
- Internet media: things we use on laptops, desktop computers, tablets, video games and PlayStation. Examples: educational websites, Qur’an apps, e-books.
- Mobile phones: used for calls, text messages, photos, videos and apps.

### How media can reinforce learning
- We can listen to and repeat Qur’an recitation from a radio, phone or computer to improve our tajwid.
- We can read stories of the prophets and the companions in books.
- We can watch educational programmes on TV.
- We can search for information for school projects on the Internet with the help of an adult.
- We can use phones to call relatives and keep family ties.

### Media are a gift from Allah
Allah (S.W.T.) gave people the mind to think and to make these tools. The first verses revealed to the Prophet (S.A.W) mention the pen: “Who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know” (Qur’an 96:4-5). A pen, a book and a computer are all tools for learning. A Muslim thanks Allah for media by using them for good.

## Key words
• media — tools and channels that carry information to many people, such as radio, TV, books and the Internet
• print media — media that are printed on paper, such as books and newspapers
• broadcast media — media sent out through the air, such as radio and television

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Sort these into types of media: newspaper, radio, laptop, television, magazine.

Working:
1. Printed on paper: newspaper, magazine.
2. Sent through the air to many people: radio, television.
3. Used for the Internet: laptop.

Answer: Print: newspaper, magazine. Broadcast: radio, television. Internet: laptop.

## Activity: Media at home
You will need: Exercise book, Pictures of different media
1. Each learner lists the media used at home.
2. In groups, sort the list into print, broadcast, Internet media and mobile phones.
3. Next to each medium, write one way it can help you learn about Islam or school work.
4. Share your table with another group.

## Practice
1. Name the four types of media named in this lesson.
2. Give two examples of print media.
3. How can a radio help a learner to learn the Qur’an?
4. Why do Muslims call media a gift from Allah?

## Summary
• Media include print, broadcast and Internet media, and mobile phones.
• Media can help us learn the Qur’an, school work and good manners.
• Media are a gift from Allah and should be used for good.

### Answers to practice
1. Print media, broadcast media, Internet media and mobile phones.
2. Any two: books, newspapers, magazines, posters, charts.
3. The learner can listen to Qur’an recitation and repeat it to improve reading.
4. Allah gave people the knowledge and mind to make them, and they help us learn.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Positive and negative uses of media

LESSON 2: POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE USES OF MEDIA
=============================================

## What you will learn
• State positive uses of media.
• State negative uses of media and their dangers.
• Explain how positive use of media builds Islamic character.

Curriculum outcomes: b) explain the positive use of media for Islamic character formation

## Introduction
A knife can be used to cut vegetables or to hurt someone. Media are the same. A phone can be used to listen to a lecture about the Prophet (S.A.W), or to watch something harmful.

## Notes
### Positive uses of media
- Learning the Qur’an, Hadith and stories of the prophets
- Getting knowledge for school and Madrasa
- Listening to good anashid (Islamic songs) and lectures
- Getting news, weather reports and important announcements
- Talking to relatives and friends, and keeping family ties
- Knowing prayer times and the start of Ramadhan and Eid

### Negative uses of media
- Watching or listening to bad pictures, bad language or violent films
- Playing video games for so long that one misses swalah, homework or sleep
- Spreading lies, rumours and gossip
- Bullying or abusing others with messages
- Talking to strangers online and giving them personal information

### Dangers of misusing media
Misuse of media wastes time, spoils good character, can teach bad behaviour and can put a child in danger. The Prophet (S.A.W) said: “There are two blessings which many people lose: health and free time.” (Bukhari)

### How positive use of media builds Islamic character
- A learner who listens to good lectures learns good manners (akhlaq).
- Using media for learning makes a person knowledgeable.
- Controlling time spent on screens teaches self-discipline.
- Checking information before sharing teaches truthfulness.

The Prophet (S.A.W) said: “Part of the goodness of a person’s Islam is leaving what does not concern him.” (Tirmidhi) A Muslim avoids media content that does not help him in this life or the next.

## Key words
• positive use — using something in a good and helpful way
• rumour — a story passed from person to person that may not be true
• anashid — Islamic songs with good messages

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Salma spends her whole Saturday playing games on her father’s phone and forgets to pray Dhuhr. Is this a positive or negative use of media? Explain.

Working:
1. She is using too much time on games.
2. She missed swalah, which is an obligation.

Answer: Negative, because it wasted her time and made her miss swalah.

## Activity: Positive or negative?
You will need: Video clips on positive use of media, Manila paper divided into two columns
1. Watch a short video clip on positive use of media.
2. In groups, write positive uses of media on one side and negative uses on the other.
3. Discuss how each negative use can harm a Muslim’s character.
4. Present your chart in class.

## Practice
1. State three positive uses of media.
2. State two negative uses of media.
3. Which two blessings did the Prophet (S.A.W) say many people lose?

## Summary
• Media are good when used for learning, communication and useful news.
• Misuse wastes time, spoils character and can be dangerous.
• Positive use of media builds knowledge, discipline and truthfulness.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: learning the Qur’an and Hadith, school learning, good lectures and anashid, news, keeping in touch with relatives, knowing prayer times.
2. Any two: watching bad content, too much gaming, spreading lies, bullying, talking to strangers online.
3. Health and free time.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Islamic manners when using media

LESSON 3: ISLAMIC MANNERS WHEN USING MEDIA
==========================================

## What you will learn
• State Islamic teachings on the use of media.
• Practise good manners when using phones, TV and the Internet.

Curriculum outcomes: c) observe Islamic ethics while using media in day-to-day life; d) appreciate media as a gift from Allah (S.W.T.) by using them appropriately

## Introduction
Someone sends a message to a class group saying school will be closed tomorrow. Should you forward it at once? Islam teaches us what to do.

## Notes
### Islamic teachings on using media
- Check news before sharing it. Allah (S.W.T.) says: “O you who believe, if a wrongdoer comes to you with news, verify it.” (Qur’an 49:6)
- Speak good or stay quiet. The Prophet (S.A.W) said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should say what is good or keep silent.” (Bukhari and Muslim) This also applies to what we type and send.
- Guard your eyes and ears. Allah says that the hearing, the sight and the heart will all be questioned (Qur’an 17:36). Do not watch or listen to indecent things.
- Do not mock, abuse or backbite others through messages or videos.
- Respect prayer times. Switch off the TV or put the phone away when it is time for swalah.
- Respect people’s privacy. Do not take or share other people’s photos without permission.

### Good manners for a Grade 4 learner
- Use a phone, computer or TV with permission from your parents.
- Agree with your parents on how much time to spend on screens.
- Never share your name, school or home address with strangers online.
- If you see something bad or frightening, switch it off and tell an adult.
- Keep the volume low so you do not disturb others.
- Begin with Bismillah and use the device for something useful.

### Appreciating media
A Muslim shows thankfulness to Allah for media by using them for good, such as learning, and by keeping away from what Allah has forbidden.

## Key words
• verify — check that something is true
• privacy — a person’s right to keep their own information and pictures to themselves
• ethics — rules of right and wrong behaviour

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Ali receives a message calling a classmate bad names and is asked to forward it. What should he do according to Islamic teachings?

Working:
1. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught us to say what is good or keep silent.
2. Forwarding the message would hurt the classmate and spread evil.

Answer: He should not forward it, and he should tell a parent or teacher.

## Activity: Listening to a resource person
You will need: A resource person such as an Imam, Madrasa teacher or parent, Exercise book
1. Prepare two questions to ask the resource person about Islamic teachings on using media.
2. Listen attentively and write down the main points.
3. In pairs, make a poster titled ‘My media rules’ with five rules you will follow.
4. Take the poster home and share it with your family.

## Practice
1. What does Qur’an 49:6 teach about news?
2. What should you do if you see something bad on a phone or TV?
3. Give three good manners of using media.

## Summary
• Check news before sharing it (Qur’an 49:6).
• Say or send only what is good; guard your eyes and ears.
• Use media with permission, for a limited time and never during swalah.

### Answers to practice
1. We should check (verify) news before believing or sharing it.
2. Switch it off and tell an adult.
3. Any three: use with permission, limit screen time, do not talk to strangers, verify news, respect prayer times, do not share others’ photos without permission, keep volume low.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.1.3 POSITIVE USAGE OF MEDIA
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these is an example of broadcast media?
   A. Newspaper
   B. Radio
   C. Book
   D. Poster

2. Which of these is print media?
   A. Television
   B. Magazine
   C. PlayStation
   D. Radio

3. Name one way a mobile phone can help a learner to learn.

4. Which is a positive use of media?
   A. Spreading rumours
   B. Watching violent films
   C. Listening to a lecture on the Seerah
   D. Playing games during swalah time

5. How does controlling screen time build good character?

6. According to Qur’an 49:6, what should a believer do when he hears news from a wrongdoer?
   A. Share it quickly
   B. Verify it
   C. Laugh at it
   D. Change it

7. The Prophet (S.A.W) said a believer should say what is good or …
   A. shout
   B. keep silent
   C. tell a joke
   D. write it down

8. A stranger online asks for your home address. What should you do?
   A. Give it
   B. Refuse and tell a parent
   C. Send a photo of your house
   D. Give your school name instead

9. What should you do with the TV when the adhan is called?

10. How does a Muslim show thankfulness to Allah for media?
   A. By using them for good
   B. By breaking them
   C. By using them all night
   D. By watching anything
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.1.3 POSITIVE USAGE OF MEDIA
========================================

1. B. Radio
   Radio and television send out programmes to many people through the air.

2. B. Magazine
   A magazine is printed on paper.

3. Any one: listening to Qur’an recitation, using a learning app, calling a teacher or relative for help, reading e-books.
   Phones used well can support learning.

4. C. Listening to a lecture on the Seerah
   Learning about the life of the Prophet (S.A.W) builds good character.

5. It teaches self-discipline and leaves time for swalah, study and family.
   Wasting free time is a loss the Prophet (S.A.W) warned about.

6. B. Verify it
   Allah commands believers to check news before acting on it.

7. B. keep silent
   This Hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim and applies to messages too.

8. B. Refuse and tell a parent
   Never share personal information with strangers online.

9. Switch it off or turn it down and go to pray.
   Swalah is more important than any programme.

10. A. By using them for good
   We thank Allah for a gift by using it the way He likes.

questions.explanation: This Hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim and applies to messages too.

questions.question: A stranger online asks for your home address. What should you do?
options: Send a photo of your house
questions.explanation: Never share personal information with strangers online.

questions.question: What should you do with the TV when the adhan is called?
questions.answer: Switch it off or turn it down and go to pray.
questions.explanation: Swalah is more important than any programme.

questions.question: How does a Muslim show thankfulness to Allah for media?
questions.explanation: We thank Allah for a gift by using it the way He likes.

curriculum.design: KICD Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION Curriculum Design (Revised 2024)

outcomes.text: identify types of media that can be used to reinforce learning
explain the positive use of media for Islamic character formation
observe Islamic ethics while using media in day-to-day life
appreciate media as a gift from Allah (S.W.T.) by using them appropriately
